answers.explanation: /20 is 255.255.240.0, block size 16 in the 3rd octet. 45 is in the block 32 to 47.
The block 32 to 47 ends at 47, so 172.16.47.255.
/25 is block size 128: .0 and .128. 130 is in the upper half.
The broadcast is .255, so the last host is .254.
Block size 32: .64 to .95 is one subnet, and .65 and .94 are both in it. .30/.33 and .95/.96 straddle a boundary, and .40 is past .31.
A /23 here is 10.0.0.0 to 10.0.1.255. 10.0.0.255 is in the middle of that range, not the broadcast. Watch out for addresses that only look like broadcasts.
2 borrowed bits: 2² = 4 subnets of 64 addresses each.
